4Reall??!
The Many Lives of Mona

From a young girl in Tamale to one of Ghana's most talked-about public figures — an intimate documentary exploring fame, identity, reinvention, reckoning, and the search for meaning beyond the image.

SubjectMona Faiz Montrage
Runtime90 Minutes
FormatFeature Documentary
OriginGhana / West Africa
Scroll
@hajia4reall
Why the title
4Reall??!
The Cultural Hook
"For real??" is what people say when something shocks them beyond belief. It is the exact question Ghana — and the world — asked when her story broke.
Her Name, Her Brand
4Reall is her stage name, her identity, the word she built an empire on. She literally called herself "real." The title takes that word and turns it into the film's central question.
The Irony
A woman who branded herself on authenticity while living a double life. 4Reall??! holds both truths at once — the name she chose and the doubt the world now attaches to it.
The Punctuation
Two question marks. One exclamation. That is precisely how anyone says it out loud when genuinely stunned. The title sounds exactly like a person speaking.

The Reckoning — Timeline
Nov 2022Arrested in the United Kingdom
May 2023Extradited to the United States
Feb 2024Pleaded guilty — romance scam proceeds, targeting elderly Americans (2013–2019)
Jun 2024Sentenced: 12 months · $1.38M restitution · 3 years supervised release
May 2025Released. Returned to Ghana. Her next chapter is unwritten.
The Film's Central Question
"Who is Mona when the image disappears — and who does she choose to become?"

Visual Language
How the film will look and feel
Tamale / Childhood
Warm amber tones. Natural light. Dust. Unhurried pacing.
The Rise
Saturated, high-contrast. Social media aesthetics. The persona being built in real time.
Glamour / Celebrity
Cinematic fashion photography. Rich lighting. The image at its most constructed.
The Reckoning
Stripped. Near-monochrome. Silence. The visual language flattens as the image does.
Reflection
Cool, measured light. Long pauses allowed. She is allowed to just be a person.
Return to Tamale
Natural light returns — richer now. Greens and earth. Home without nostalgia.

What this film is really about
Six Themes.
One Human Story.
◎
Identity & Reinvention
Who are we when we're no longer who the world thinks we are? The film asks which version of Mona is real.
◈
The Construction of Celebrity
How a persona is manufactured in the social media age — and the gap between image and person.
◇
Ambition at Any Cost
A girl from Tamale who studied fashion in New York and built multiple companies. The cost of wanting more.
◉
African Luxury Culture
A generation's relationship with sudden wealth and the silence around its origins.
△
Tamale & the North
Northern Ghana as place, identity, and gravity. No matter how far she went, Tamale remained her centre.
○
Accountability Without a Neat Ending
Not a redemption arc. A genuinely unresolved question held honestly — without resolving the tension artificially.

Director's Vision
Why this story.
Why now.
Why this way.
"This film is not about celebrity gossip or headlines. It is not a takedown, and it is not a rehabilitation. It is something harder and more honest than either — an attempt to sit with a human being who has lived many lives, some glamorous, some damaging, some still unresolved, and ask the question the image never allowed: who are you, really?"
— Tiah Alidu, Director & Producer
Timing
Freshly back from prison. Story still live. This is not a retrospective — it is a document of an unfinished human journey.
Access
Mona has agreed to participate. This is a collaboration — the depth of honesty is in her hands, and we intend to help her find it.
Moral Complexity
We hold both her humanity and the consequences of her choices — without resolving the tension artificially.
Cultural Specificity
This is a story about Ghana, about the North, about Tamale. That specificity is the source of its global resonance.
"The world knows the image. This film tells the story."
